_comment: Favicon provenance. The artwork is the CDN's canonical .ico, but it is served from this origin because the CDN blocks it — see cdn_hotlink_block.

root_mirror.why: Serves the declared icon and also answers the implicit /favicon.ico root request browsers make regardless of declarations. Byte-identical to the CDN canonical asset, so it cannot drift in appearance.

apple_touch_icon.why: Not available on the CDN, and Safari does not accept SVG for apple-touch-icon — this is what was missing on iOS. Derived from frame [3] (256x256) of the canonical .ico, resized to 180x180 with alpha removed, because iOS composites it onto the home screen and ignores transparency.

note: The nav logo also loads from the CDN, deliberately. That was never the defect.

cdn_hotlink_block.symptom: 403 Cloudflare error 1011 for any request carrying a cross-site Referer; 200 with no Referer.
cdn_hotlink_block.why_it_matters: Browsers always send a Referer when fetching a favicon declared on a page, so this URL cannot render as a page icon. Verified in Chrome: identical bytes load from this origin and time out from the CDN, while the CDN logo SVG loads fine.
cdn_hotlink_block.scope: Path-specific. /pacs008/v1/logos/ has a hotlink bypass, which is why the nav logo works.
cdn_hotlink_block.to_serve_from_the_cdn: Add /pacs008/v1/favicon.ico to the Cloudflare hotlink-protection bypass, then this declaration can point at the CDN.

replaced_stale_icon: The previously committed static/favicon.ico was a different, older logo — a teal sunburst rather than the current waves-and-sun mark — so the live root favicon was stale artwork as well as the declarations being broken.
